- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline, reduce forecasted price by 5–15% to account for risk aversion.  
- If sentiment remains high for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 3–8% to prevent overshoot.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 10–20% in next 5–7 days.  
- If news volume drops below 2.0 for 2+ consecutive days, model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to reflect reduced market activity.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10%.  
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model often overreacts; apply 5–10% downward correction to avoid volatility overestimation.
